record.paper_title: Some open problems in the theory of analytic multifunctions
record.original_question: Let D be a plane domain. Suppose K1 and K2 are analytic multifunctions on D whose values are sequences tending to zero. If K1 = K2 on a subset of D having a limit point in D, must K1 and K2 be identical on all of D?

evidence.quote: Problem F. Let K1 and K2 be analytic multifunctions on D whose values are sequences tending to zero. If K1 = K2 on a set with a limit point in D, must we have K1 equiv K2 on D?
As far as we know, this problem is still open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $c_0$ denote the Banach space of real (or complex) sequences converging to zero, equipped with the supremum norm. A set-valued map $K$ defined on a plane domain $D \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ that assigns to each $\lambda \in D$ a nonempty compact subset $K(\lambda) \subset c_0$ is called an analytic multifunction on $D$ if it is upper semicontinuous and if, for every plurisubharmonic function $\varphi$ on $c_0$, the function $\lambda \mapsto \sup\{\varphi(x) : x \in K(\lambda)\}$ is subharmonic on $D$.

Suppose $K_1$ and $K_2$ are two analytic multifunctions on $D$ whose values are compact subsets of $c_0$ (i.e., compact sets of sequences tending to zero). Assume that the set $\{\lambda \in D : K_1(\lambda) = K_2(\lambda)\}$ has a limit point in $D$.

Must it follow that $K_1(\lambda) = K_2(\lambda)$ for every $\lambda \in D$?
artifact.status_search_result: A survey listing open problems in the theory of analytic multifunctions states this question as Problem F and notes that, to the authors' knowledge, it remains open. While an identity principle is known for analytic multifunctions valued in $\ell^p$-sequences with locally bounded $\ell^p$-norms, the analogous statement for $c_0$-valued multifunctions has not been established.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems in the theory of analytic multifunctions
status_evidence.snippet: Problem F asks whether two analytic multifunctions valued in c_0 that agree on a set with a limit point in D must coincide on D; the authors note this problem is still open.
status_evidence.claim: The c_0-valued identity principle for analytic multifunctions is stated as an open problem.
